title: Successor step for formal smoothness of a Cohen ring modulo p powers
statement: Let p be prime and Λ a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Let n≥1 and suppose that Λ/(p^n) is formally smooth over ZMod (p^n) for every ZMod-algebra structure. Then Λ/(p^(n+1)) is formally smooth over ZMod (p^(n+1)) for every such algebra structure.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step, applying Tag 031L; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/031L

proof.text: Apply cohenRing_mod_pow_flat to Λ/(p^(n+1)) with its given ZMod(p^(n+1))-algebra structure. This supplies the flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: Let R=ZMod(p^(n+1)), S=Λ/(p^(n+1)), I=(p^n) in R, and J=IS. Ideal.span_singleton_pow identifies I² with the ideal generated by p^(2n). Since n≥1, n+1≤2n, so ZMod.natCast_pow_eq_zero_of_le makes this generator zero.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: Apply modPow_formallySmooth_reduction with m=n+1 to the induction hypothesis; it yields formal smoothness of the actual induced map R/I→S/J.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: Apply RingHom.FormallySmooth.of_flat_of_ker_eq_map_of_square_zero. The quotient maps are surjective, the square commutes by definition, and their kernels are I and J by Ideal.mk_ker. The result is formal smoothness of the given algebra map R→S; RingHom.formallySmooth_algebraMap gives the original conclusion.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

lean.statement:
theorem cohenRing_mod_pow_formallySmooth_step
    (p : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] (hΛ : IsCohenRing p Λ)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (ih : ∀ [Algebra (ZMod (p ^ n)) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ n})],
      Algebra.FormallySmooth (ZMod (p ^ n)) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ n})) :
    ∀ [Algebra (ZMod (p ^ (n + 1))) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ (n + 1)})],
      Algebra.FormallySmooth (ZMod (p ^ (n + 1)))
        (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ (n + 1)})
